match.reason: The closest bank point, Properties of hydrocarbons, covers only chain length and dispersion forces in non-polar hydrocarbons, while the new point is broader, covering stronger forces between organic molecules generally and also melting point and viscosity.

draft.title: Boiling points of organic compounds
card: To boil a liquid, energy must pull its molecules apart from each other. The stronger the forces between molecules, the more energy is needed, so the boiling point is higher.
Longer chains have more electrons and more surface contact, so their dispersion forces are stronger. Within a family, boiling point, melting point and viscosity rise as chain length increases.
Different families have different forces. Dispersion forces are weakest, dipole-dipole forces are stronger, and hydrogen bonds (from O-H or N-H groups) are stronger again.

For molecules of similar size, an alcohol or carboxylic acid boils at a higher temperature than an alkane, because it can form hydrogen bonds. Viscosity, how slowly a liquid flows, rises with stronger forces in the same way.
draft.remember: Stronger forces between molecules mean more energy to separate them, so a higher boiling point.

a.q: Why does pentane boil at a higher temperature than propane?
opts: Its longer chain gives stronger dispersion forces
Its longer chain gives it hydrogen bonds
Its covalent bonds are stronger within each molecule
Its molecules are more polar than propane molecules
a.why: Pentane has more electrons and a longer chain, so its dispersion forces between molecules are stronger and more energy is needed to separate them. Hydrogen bonds need O-H or N-H groups, which neither alkane has.
a.clue: Both are alkanes, so think about chain length and the forces between molecules.

b.q: Ethanol (CH3CH2OH) and propane (CH3CH2CH3) have similar molar masses. Why does ethanol have the much higher boiling point?
opts: Ethanol molecules form hydrogen bonds with each other
Ethanol has a longer carbon chain than propane
Ethanol has stronger covalent bonds inside its molecules
Ethanol has only dispersion forces between its molecules
b.why: Ethanol has an O-H group, so its molecules form hydrogen bonds, which are stronger than the dispersion forces between propane molecules. More energy is needed to separate ethanol molecules. The chain lengths are similar, so chain length does not explain the gap.
b.clue: Look at the functional group on ethanol that propane lacks.

a.best: Its longer chain gives stronger dispersion forces

b.best: Ethanol molecules form hydrogen bonds with each other
